title: Personalized Policy Learning through Discrete Experimentation
claim: Users on the platform earn and redeem discrete point-based incentives through familiar app screens, which defines the setting where continuous policies must be set.
layout: 3 phone screenshots side by side, left-to-right, labeled (a)-(c)
description: Three smartphone mockups sit side by side, labeled (a), (b) and (c), all showing a social media app in white, gray and red. (a) is a profile page with an avatar placeholder, a username, follower counts, and 'Set up Profile' and 'My Wallet' buttons. (b) is the 'My Wallet' screen. It shows a balance of 0.00 with coupon, points and bank account counts. The 'Points Redeem' tab is active. It lists red coupon tiles ($0.05, $0.1, 5% off, $1) with the points each costs (500, 900). (c) is the same wallet with the 'Points Earning Task' tab active. It lists tasks with red 'Activate' buttons and point rewards: link bank account +128, post a video +178, complete verification +538, turn on notification +58. The eye goes first to the red buttons and tiles.
caption: Illustration of the ‘Point” System on Platform
abstract: While Randomized controlled trials (RCTs), or A/B tests, are the gold standard for optimizing online-platform policies, they are limited by discrete testing levels. This approach is suboptimal for continuous variables (e.g., prices and incentives), as it fails to extrapolate to untested values or account for user heterogeneity. We address this by developing Deep Learning for Policy Targeting (\textsf{DLPT}) to learn personalized continuous policies from discrete RCTs using high-dimensional features. We prove our estimators are asymptotically unbiased and consistent, achieving a $\sqrt{n}$-regret bound. In a collaboration with a leading social media platform to optimize creator incentives, we show that \textsf{DLPT} substantially outperforms existing benchmarks.
